sources.entry: Kyoo - Innovative media browser designed for seamless streaming of anime, series and movies, offering advanced features like dynamic transcoding, auto watch history and intelligent metadata retrieval. (Demo) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Kyoo is a self-hosted media server for movies, series and anime that aims to work without a required folder structure or manual metadata edits.
summary.what_it_does: Kyoo positions itself as an alternative to Jellyfin or Plex and focuses on video content. It advertises dynamic transcoding to any quality, including adaptive bitrate switching and original quality. It scans media without requiring a particular folder layout, and claims to handle poorly named files, including anime. It offers video preview thumbnails on the progress bar, intro and credit detection via audio fingerprinting or chapter title matching, and subtitle support for PGS/VOBSUB and SSA/ASS with embedded fonts. Supported clients listed are Web, Android and Chromecast; Android TV is planned. The project is split into multiple services that can run separately, and the README says third-party apps can use them (for example, Meelo uses its transcoder). Watch-list sync and offline download are marked as removed for now, pending reimplementation in v5.
how_to_run: See the Installation documentation linked in the README for setup, OIDC and hardware transcoding instructions
notable: No folder structure required; messy filenames are meant to still scan correctly
Intro/credit detection via audio fingerprinting or chapter title matching
Split into independent services that third-party apps can reuse
Official Helm chart for Kubernetes deployment
Subtitle support for PGS, VOBSUB, SSA and ASS with embedded fonts
caveats: Developed by a single person, so few clients are available
Android TV support is planned but not yet available
Watch list sync and offline download are removed for now and not yet reimplemented in v5
Targets servers (postgres, multiple services), so it is heavier than a simple single-binary media server
